\lcCategory{With the paper's hypotheses; Lean proves a narrower conclusion.}{12}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}{2.3.1} & Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails\newline{\footnotesize Only the upper bounds of \lcRef{Equation}{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}{2.3.3} are proved (any measurable multiplier in $[0,1]$, measurable domains $S\subset S'$); its lower bounds are stated only for the full and tail domains without a multiplier, and the remarks that Gaussian smoothing gives such multipliers and keeps the $N_0$ mass identity are not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}{4.1.2} & Auxiliary mask norm\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves, under \lcRef{Hypothesis}{H:homog}{1.2.1} and $\Gamma\neq0$, that $\nu_R$ is even, tempered and Radon, the ball bound \lcRef{Equation}{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}{4.1.5} uniformly in $R>0$, and \lcRef{Equation}{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}{4.1.6} for a separable complex Hilbert space $H$ (indeed any complex Banach space) with integrability and a finite right side; the clause for a real $H$ after complexification is not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:variational-global-mean}{7.3.2} & Global regularity of the original mean\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves the display \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-global-mean}{7.3.3} on $I=[0,1]$ ($0\le h_s\le M$ and $\|h_s-h_t\|_\infty\le C_\Psi|s-t|$, with integrability, continuity in $x$ and a joint Lipschitz bound); the first sentence, that every mixed time and space derivative of $h_s$ is globally bounded, is not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-unmasked-rate}{7.3.3} & The unmasked Rayleigh rate\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves, with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, the statements about the Rayleigh supremum \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-real-rayleigh}{7.3.4}: for $\lambda$ defined as its square root, a uniform positive floor, the Lipschitz bounds and $I_\Psi$ positive and finite; the operator statements ($H_s$ self-adjoint, form domain $H^1$, spectral bottom $E_s$, $\lambda=\sqrt{-E_s}$) are not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:variational-control-dilation}{7.3.5} & Radon and Rayleigh dilation\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves the bijection and the four identities with the section's hypotheses (\lcRef{Hypothesis}{H:homog}{1.2.1}, $\Gamma\neq0$, $a=\alpha_0$) and nothing supplied, for the variance in its integral form and the rate defined as the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-real-rayleigh}{7.3.4}; their identification with $\E W(\Psi)^2$ (\lcRef{Lemma}{L:compact-raw-profile}{6.3.6}) and $\sqrt{-E_s}$ (\lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-unmasked-rate}{7.3.3}) is not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:spatial-static-controls}{8.2.2} & Smooth temporal controls\newline{\footnotesize $\lambda$ is the square root of the supremum of the real Rayleigh quotient, and $I_\Psi$, $v_\Psi$ are given by their integral formulas (identification with $\sqrt{-E_s}$ and $\E W(\Psi)^2$ is not formalized); \lcRef{Equation}{E:spatial-static-score}{8.2.2} is proved in the form that every number below the bound is exceeded by some admissible score; its supremum form assumes the boundedness claim of \lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-positive-scores}{7.3.6}.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:spatial-fourier-bound}{8.2.3} & Deterministic Fourier bound for the spatial energy\newline{\footnotesize The bound is proved with the constant $\mathcal{R}_\Gamma(1)=\int\mu(\ud\xi)/(1+|\xi|^2)$ in place of $R_\alpha$ of \lcRef{Equation}{E:intro-spectral-mass}{1.5.1}; the identity $\mathcal{R}_\Gamma(1)=R_\alpha$, which the lemma takes from the resolvent calculation in the proof of \lcRef{Lemma}{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}{2.3.1}, is not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}{8.2.4} & The finite smooth spatial ratio\newline{\footnotesize \lcRef{Equation}{E:spatial-smooth-score}{8.2.4} is proved in the form that every $y$ below the bound is exceeded by some $I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2$ ($\lambda$ the square root of the supremum of the real Rayleigh quotient, $v_\Psi$ given by its integral formula); its form as a supremum rests on a named input, the boundedness claim of \lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-positive-scores}{7.3.6}. $R_0<\infty$ is proved without that input, by \lcRef{Lemma}{L:spatial-fourier-bound}{8.2.3}.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:spatial-four-linear}{8.2.5} & The physical four-linear extension\newline{\footnotesize Joint continuity of $C_4$ on $(H^1)^4$ is proved along convergent sequences ($H^1$ convergence of the four profiles, that is $L^2$ convergence of each function and of its weak gradient), not for a topology on $(H^1)^4$; continuity of $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and of the square pairings is not restated separately (they are $C_4(f,f,f,f)$ and $C_4(f,f,h,h)$).}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:spatial-energy-map}{8.2.6} & The spatial energy and static lower variational expression\newline{\footnotesize \lcRef{Equation}{E:spatial-static-energy-score}{8.2.10} is proved in an existential form (every $y$ below $M_a^{-1/k}F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}})$ is exceeded by some $I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2$, with $\lambda$ the square root of the Rayleigh supremum \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-real-rayleigh}{7.3.4} and $v_\Psi$ by its integral formula); the supremum form assumes the boundedness claim of \lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-positive-scores}{7.3.6}.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:occupation-physical-class}{8.2.8} & The full physical occupation class\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves measurability, independence of the representatives, \lcRef{Equation}{E:occupation-physical-bound}{8.2.13} (with $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$) and \lcRef{Equation}{E:occupation-own-energy}{8.2.14} (with $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}$) over the class $\mathcal{O}$ modelled by fields with jointly measurable representatives of $g$ and of its gradient; the construction of such representatives from strongly $H^1$-measurable fields (a simple-function approximation) and the converse are not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:tube-rayleigh-tail}{10.2.7} & Exact Rayleigh tail bound\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves the bound with integrability and the finite head integral; the ``In particular'' application to the coarse-envelope bound of another proposition is not formalized.}
\end{lcTable}
